problem: Internal architecture of 'region_coordinator' (type: Service — A deployable runtime component that handles requests, performs work, or coordinates other components). Node: Global control plane for multi-region semantics: (a) aggregates per-tenant and per-tenant_cluster quota and cost counters across regions on a sub-second cadence and propagates throttle flags, plan-change tombstones, cluster-level throttle / suspension flags, key revocations, preservation holds, and erasure tombstones ahead of fine-grained counter replication via a unified fast-path; (b) computes a single canonical-tip view per (chain, fork) by quorum across regional chain pools, excluding votes from pools currently in tip-stale state, and emits coherent rollback notifications keyed on chain coordinates; (c) publishes each tenant's residency policy so edge, tenant_store, usage_meter, and metrics_store enforce it consistently; (d) distributes a hybrid-logical clock used by gateway and fanout in place of wall-clock for ordering and rate-limit bucketing. Gates lifecycle events globally so they cannot collide: cert and origin-endpoint rotations are region-staggered (no two regions transition the same surface in the same maintenance window); chain pool blue/green rotations are gated to one pool / one region / one wave at a time with the canonical-tip quorum size held above its safe threshold throughout; rotation events are tagged so chain_router's schema-skew and tip-divergence quarantines suppress noise during the documented rotation window. Coordinates tenant offboarding teardown end-to-end: on receipt of an erasure tombstone, signals gateway to close subscriptions, fanout to drop them, address_index to tombstone watch claims, chain_router to cancel in-flight long-RPCs, usage_meter to freeze the cost record, then collects per-component offboarding attestations into the compliance audit trail. Logically a single global service; physically deployed as a quorum across regions so it is not itself a SPOF. Inter-region channel is a cert-bearing surface enumerated in cert-inventory. Connections: usage_meter --calls-> region_coordinator; region_coordinator --reads_from-> tenant_store; fanout --calls-> region_coordinator; chain_router --calls-> region_coordinator; edge --calls-> region_coordinator; gateway --calls-> region_coordinator; region_coordinator --writes_to-> auth_cache. Parent requirements: R-cert-rotation-staggered: Region-staggered rotation: region_coordinator gates rotation roll-out across regions so that no two regions can transition the same surface inside the same maintenance window. Simultaneous expiry across regions is prevented by construction, not by deployment discipline.; R-rotation-coordinator-gate: region_coordinator gates pool-rotation events globally: at most one pool, one region, one rotation wave at a time, and the canonical-tip quorum size is held above its safe threshold throughout. Rotations are scheduled, not ad-hoc.; R-stale-pool-quorum-exclusion: region_coordinator's canonical-tip quorum excludes votes from any chain pool currently in tip-stale state, so a stalled regional pool cannot anchor the global canonical-tip view.; R-origin-rotation: Origin endpoints (the IP/hostname pairs gateway accepts on) rotate on a documented cadence under region_coordinator's gating, neutralizing leaked-origin windows; rotation is region-staggered like cert rotation so no two regions rotate simultaneously.; R-per-fork-canonical-tip: region_coordinator maintains a separate canonical-tip per (chain, fork) and reports it as such. Tenants explicitly subscribe to or query a (chain, fork) pair; the protocol-version surface advertises which forks are currently supported.; R-offboarding-teardown: Tenant offboarding triggers a documented end-to-end teardown coordinated by region_coordinator: open subscriptions closed with a structured reason, fanout state dropped, address_index watches removed, in-flight long-RPCs cancelled, usage_meter cost record frozen at offboarding time. Each component emits an offboarding attestation collected into the compliance audit trail.

stressors.description: A network partition isolates a minority of regions from the quorum (e.g. one of three regions, or a transit failure leaves a 1/5 island). Subservices in the minority region continue receiving inputs (usage_meter deltas, chain_router head observations, erasure tombstones from local tenant_store) but cannot commit through quorum_core. The partition lasts long enough that buffered local work would overflow if held, but short enough that a hard failover would cause inconsistencies on heal.
stressors.attractor: Minority-region subservices buffer locally until OOM (memory exhaustion / disk fill), or fail-fast every input with no fallback. On heal, the buffered work is replayed without ordering or idempotency guarantees, causing duplicate flags / duplicate aggregates / out-of-order tip updates.
stressors.solution: Minority regions enter a documented partition-degraded mode: (a) reads are served from locally-applied state_log with a 'partition-stale' freshness annotation; (b) proposals from minority regions are rejected fast with a retryable-on-quorum-region signal so upstream can shed load via region_coordinator's edge integration; (c) inputs that cannot be discarded (usage_meter deltas, chain_router head observations, erasure tombstones from local tenant_store) are buffered with a bounded watermark and explicit overflow policy (drop-with-loss-attestation for low-severity, escalate to alert for high-severity); (d) on heal, buffered work is replayed via quorum_core with idempotency keys so duplicates land but only commit once.

stressors.description: state_log accumulates indefinitely: every throttle tombstone, plan-change, key-revocation, residency-policy version, canonical-tip update, rotation event, HLC sample, and offboarding attestation. Years of operation. There is no compaction story in the naive design — eventually replication catch-up, replica cold-start, and crash-recovery times grow without bound, and disk fills.
stressors.attractor: state_log grows monotonically; replication catch-up time, cold-start time, and disk usage all grow without bound. Eventually replicas can never recover from cold start within an SLO; new regions cannot be added without weeks-long bootstrap.
stressors.solution: Per-class retention/compaction policy: each entry kind in state_log declares its retention class. Tip updates compact aggressively (only the latest committed canonical tip per (chain, fork) plus a bounded reorg-window history); HLC samples retain only the last per-region observation; quota aggregates compact to per-period summaries; tombstones (revocation, plan-change, cluster-suspended, preservation-hold, erasure) retain full history under a snapshot-and-truncate scheme — snapshots are taken at watermark intervals and the prefix is truncated, so any replica catches up via snapshot + log-tail; rotation events compact post-completion. quorum_core implements snapshot+truncate with replica catch-up via snapshot transfer.

stressors.description: All write classes go through the same single state_log: high-frequency canonical-tip updates (one per chain block per chain × number of forks), high-frequency quota-aggregate snapshots, low-frequency but latency-critical throttle and erasure tombstones, and rotation events. During a chain reorg or a metering surge, tip writes and quota writes saturate consensus throughput; latency-critical revocation/throttle tombstones queue behind them — flag_propagator's fast-path is no longer fast.
stressors.attractor: All write classes serialize through a single state_log; under load, latency-critical tombstones (throttle, revocation, cluster-suspension, erasure) queue behind high-frequency tip updates and quota snapshots. The 'fast-path' for flag propagation is no longer fast; SLA on suspension propagation is missed; abuse and revocation windows widen.
stressors.solution: Split state_log into write-class lanes with reserved consensus throughput and an explicit per-lane SLO. Lane assignment is by entry kind: a tombstone-lane (small, latency-critical: throttle, revocation, plan-change, cluster-suspended, preservation-hold, erasure), a tip-lane (high-frequency tip updates and rollback events), an aggregate-lane (quota summaries, HLC samples), a control-lane (residency-policy versions, rotation events, attestations). Each lane is its own quorum stream sharing the quorum_core engine but with reserved bandwidth and head-of-line isolation. Cross-lane causal ordering is via HLC stamps.

stressors.description: A misbehaving or compromised chain_router replica in one region spams tip_quorum with high-frequency, high-cardinality fake head observations (different fake fork ids, rapidly-changing fake tips). The naive design has no per-source rate limit on observation submissions and treats every reported fork as a candidate (chain, fork) pair. tip_quorum's working set explodes; legitimate head observations are starved.
stressors.attractor: tip_quorum's working set explodes with high-cardinality fake (chain, fork) candidates; legitimate head observations starve; canonical-tip computation latency rises; legitimate forks are masked by adversarial noise.
stressors.solution: Per-source observation rate limits at tip_quorum's input boundary; head observations are authenticated via the parent cert-bearing surface and tagged with their source replica identity. (chain, fork_id) admission requires N independent regional observations across a documented window before becoming a candidate fork pair (multi-source admission threshold). Sources whose observation pattern violates rate or cross-source-correlation rules are quarantined the same way chain_router quarantines a divergent-tip replica; quarantines surface as fork-detected alerts so operators distinguish 'legitimate emerging fork' from 'misbehaving source'.

stressors.description: One region's hlc_service replica receives wildly-wrong inter-region HLC samples (clock-source bug, time-config mismatch, malicious-peer scenario). The naive distribution accepts any peer-reported sample. Either the bad sample is propagated and inflates HLC globally — invalidating rate-limit windows and breaking ordering — or the bad region is ejected from sample exchange and silently drifts away from the rest.
stressors.attractor: Either bad samples propagate and inflate global HLC (invalidating rate-limit windows and ordering), or the bad region's hlc_service is silently ejected and drifts away — both regimes break R-bounded-clock-skew at parent scope.
stressors.solution: HLC sample acceptance is bounded: any peer-reported sample beyond max-allowed-delta from the local HLC is discarded, the source is flagged, and the local hlc_service does not advance from that sample. Cross-region HLC consensus uses multi-peer agreement (median of N peer samples, where N >= 3) rather than any-single-peer trust. A region whose hlc_service cannot produce a sample within max-delta of multi-peer median for a documented window is automatically forced into the parent-defined skew-degraded mode and stops accepting writes that depend on time-bucketed enforcement.

stressors.description: An erasure tombstone fires for tenant T. offboarding_orchestrator signals gateway, fanout, address_index, chain_router, usage_meter. One downstream component is in a degraded state and never returns its attestation (or returns 'pending' indefinitely). The naive design waits for all attestations before forwarding the certificate of deletion. Erasure can never be declared complete; legal/compliance commitments time out.
stressors.attractor: Erasure can never be declared complete; legal/compliance commitments time out; tenant data persists past lawful retention because one component never attests.
stressors.solution: Per-component attestation timeout with documented escalation path: each downstream component has an SLO for returning its attestation. On timeout, offboarding_orchestrator captures a 'best-effort attestation' with documented evidence (last-known-state, log references, escalation owner) and proposes it via quorum_core. The aggregate certificate of deletion can be issued in 'complete-with-exceptions' state when all timely attestations land plus all timeouts have best-effort attestations; exceptions are tracked in a separate exception register and have their own SLA on resolution. Erasure-preservation conflicts (parent R-preservation-hold) take precedence: a held data class blocks erasure attestation with a documented reason.

stressors.description: lifecycle_gate's check 'is canonical-tip quorum size above the safe threshold?' is read against the locally-applied state_log view. By the time the rotation is admitted and propagated, a separate region's pool has gone tip-stale (e.g. due to an upstream chain_router fault), and the actual quorum size is now below threshold. The naive 'check then admit' is not atomic with the state used for the check.
stressors.attractor: Rotation admitted while quorum size is actually below safe threshold; canonical-tip computation degrades during rotation; client-visible inconsistency in canonical-tip view.
stressors.solution: Rotation admission is itself a quorum_core proposal that includes its own preconditions as a CAS payload (current per-(chain, fork) quorum-size set, current rotation-in-progress set, current tip-stale set). At commit time, consensus re-validates the preconditions against the latest applied state; if any precondition has changed, the proposal is rejected and lifecycle_gate must re-evaluate. This makes admission atomic with the state used for the check.

stressors.description: A tenant's residency policy changes (EU-only -> EU+US). residency_publisher writes the new version via quorum_core and starts pushing to consumers. During the push window, an in-flight request reaches a US-region gateway that hasn't yet received the new version — but for a tenant whose previous policy was 'EU-only'. With the naive 'push and apply when received' model, there is a window in which the US gateway either rejects requests that the new policy now permits (false-deny, harmless) or — when the change is in the other direction (relaxing -> tightening) — the consumer still serves out-of-policy traffic until the push lands.
stressors.attractor: Either over-permissive window (out-of-policy traffic served) or under-permissive window (false-deny noise). The over-permissive direction is the residency-violation regime — a regulatory hazard.
stressors.solution: Residency policies are versioned and consumers pin the policy_version they applied to outgoing requests; downstream re-checks the version and rejects on mismatch. residency_publisher commits each new policy version to state_log with an effective-from HLC stamp. For tightening changes (narrowing allowed regions), residency_publisher uses a two-phase apply: phase 1 commits the new version with effective-from in the future (push-and-acknowledge window), phase 2 activates the version. Until activation, consumers continue to enforce the old version; the activation moment is globally-ordered via HLC. Consumers that have not acknowledged readiness within the push-window default to the deny-by-default behavior for the affected tenant.

stressors.description: A new entry kind is added to state_log (say, a new tombstone class for a new abuse signal). A rolling upgrade across regions has, mid-upgrade, replicas at version N and version N+1 in the same quorum. A new entry written by an N+1 leader is unreadable by N replicas. The naive design has no schema versioning on state_log entries; the cluster halts consensus or skews state until the upgrade completes.
stressors.attractor: Mid-upgrade quorum mixes versions; new entries are unreadable by old replicas. Either consensus halts (safe but unavailable) or replicas silently skip entries (unsafe — divergent state).
stressors.solution: state_log entries are tagged with schema_version. quorum_core's leader admits a new schema_version only after a capability-negotiation step (analogous to Raft membership change): a config entry committed via quorum that signals 'version >= V supported across all replicas'; until that config entry commits, leaders restrict writes to the previous schema_version. Replica upgrades are gated by lifecycle_gate (region-staggered, like cert rotation) so the schema-capability config entry can be committed only when every replica has been upgraded. This is a two-phase upgrade: roll out new code (idle), then commit the capability bump (active).

stressors.description: Operator wants to drain a region for planned maintenance (kernel upgrade, data-center work). Draining a region drops one of its chain pool's votes from tip_quorum and may briefly drop a region's quorum_core replica. lifecycle_gate's rule 'only admit pool rotations while canonical-tip quorum size is above its safe threshold' denies any pool rotation in any other region during the drain. There is also no explicit gate for 'admit operator-initiated region drain'; planned maintenance and global pool rotation interlock and starve each other.
stressors.attractor: Region drains and pool rotations interlock and starve each other; planned maintenance windows extend; rotation backlog accumulates.
stressors.solution: Region-drain is modeled as a first-class lifecycle event (distinct entry kind, not piggybacked on pool rotation). lifecycle_gate computes its quorum-size threshold drain-aware: the threshold is evaluated against the post-drain configuration so the gate does not block rotations purely because a drain is in progress, but also does not admit rotations that would drop the post-drain quorum below safe. Drains and rotations have an explicit mutual scheduling rule: at most one drain plus one pool rotation in flight globally, and the two events are admitted via the same CAS proposal mechanism (SR1-rotation-cas-admission) so admission is atomic against the latest configuration.

stressors.description: An abuse-driven cluster suspension is committed via quorum_core. flag_propagator's fast-path is bounded by a per-region delivery latency. A sophisticated abuser anticipates the suspension and shifts traffic to a region that has not yet received the cluster-suspended flag. Naive flag_propagator has no upper bound on per-region delivery skew, no cross-region 'flag-applied' acknowledgement, and no fallback to deny-by-default for cluster ids in the propagation window.
stressors.attractor: Suspended cluster shifts traffic to lagging region during the propagation window; suspension is bypassed for a measurable interval; abuse signal-to-action loop is broken.
stressors.solution: flag_propagator's per-region delivery latency for the unified fast-path has a documented SLO that is monitored independently. For high-severity flags (cluster-suspended, key-revocation, erasure-tombstone), flag_propagator publishes a 'flag-pending-cluster-id' marker to every region's auth_cache before the per-region apply lands; auth_cache treats pending markers as deny-during-propagation for the affected cluster_id. Per-region apply produces an explicit 'flag-applied' attestation written back via quorum_core; a flag is considered globally-active only after attestations from every region land. Regions whose flag-apply lags exceed SLO are surfaced as alerts.

stressors.description: After a quorum_core leader change, an offboarding_orchestrator instance retries unconfirmed attestation proposals and downstream signals. Without idempotency keys, downstream components (gateway, fanout, address_index, chain_router, usage_meter) may double-process: attempt to close already-closed subscriptions, double-decrement counters, return inconsistent attestations. The aggregate certificate of deletion captures duplicate evidence and is hard to audit.
stressors.attractor: After leader change, retried offboarding signals cause double-teardown effects downstream; aggregate certificate captures duplicates; audit trail is corrupted.
stressors.solution: Every offboarding signal carries an idempotency key (offboarding_id, component_id, attempt_id) and is committed via quorum_core's tombstone-lane so the canonical signal record survives leader change. Downstream components treat repeated keys as the same logical request: they return the same attestation for the same key (cached). offboarding_orchestrator dedupes incoming attestations by key before aggregating into the certificate of deletion. Leader change does not produce duplicate downstream effects — at-most-once observable behavior with at-least-once delivery.

stressors.description: CAS retry storm under leader churn: repeated lifecycle_gate / quota_aggregator CAS rejections ping-pong with leader election; forward progress stalls without backoff or admission control
stressors.attractor: Repeated CAS rejection + leader churn cause unbounded retry; system-wide live-lock with 100% consensus throughput consumed by re-proposals; rotations and quota throttle decisions never commit
stressors.solution: Add CAS-aware backoff and admission control: CAS proposers must apply exponential backoff with jitter on rejection; quorum_core enforces per-proposer in-flight CAS budget; on leader change, in-flight CAS proposals from previous leader are returned with a transient-error code that triggers backoff rather than immediate retry

stressors.description: Snapshot transfer half-applied during replica restart: replica crashes mid-snapshot; partial state left on disk; rejoin must distinguish 'fresh cold' from 'half-applied dirty' or it serves corrupted reads / commits inconsistent state
stressors.attractor: Replica rejoins quorum, applies remaining log on top of half-written snapshot, votes on proposals against silently-corrupt local state; quorum can advance with one replica diverged
stressors.solution: Atomic snapshot install with intent record: replica writes a 'snapshot-installing' intent record before any state mutation; on restart, presence of intent without commit-marker triggers full discard and re-fetch from quorum; replica refuses to participate in quorum until snapshot install completes (rotates to NEEDS_SNAPSHOT state)

stressors.description: Deny-during-propagation as DoS: adversary triggers high-severity flag-pending repeatedly to deny legitimate traffic during propagation window; flag_propagator publishes pending-markers without rate limiting or scoping
stressors.attractor: Repeated pending-markers for a target tenant_cluster cause sustained deny-by-default in auth_cache; legitimate traffic blocked even though no flag actually commits; effectively a denial of service amplified through the fast-path
stressors.solution: Pending-marker rate limiting and origin attribution: pending-markers are scoped by (target_identity, originating_proposal_id); flag_propagator enforces a per-target_identity pending-marker rate; pending-markers published without a corresponding committed-or-in-flight tombstone proposal are rejected; markers auto-expire on a documented bound and require explicit refresh tied to a live proposal

stressors.description: Probationary fork-pool starvation: legitimate emerging fork stays probationary indefinitely because N independent regional observations cannot accumulate (asymmetric chain_router rollout, regional outage, censoring); no timeout or operator-override path
stressors.attractor: Real fork visible to N-1 regions never admitted to canonical-tip view; subscribers querying that fork see stale data; no escape valve when threshold cannot be met for legitimate operational reasons
stressors.solution: Probationary timeout with operator-override path: probationary fork candidates carry a documented max-probationary-window after which tip_quorum surfaces an alert listing observed-region-set and absent-region-set; an operator-override CAS proposal via lifecycle_gate can admit a probationary fork over the threshold-shortfall provided drain/rotation states justify the missing regions; the override is itself committed in tip_lane with attribution

stressors.description: aggregate_lane back-pressure: usage_meter delta arrival rate exceeds aggregate_lane consensus throughput sustained; quota_aggregator's input buffer overflows or arbitrarily delays throttle-flag proposals to tombstone_lane
stressors.attractor: Sustained delta rate causes growing in-buffer; either OOM, or per-tenant deltas dropped silently; throttle-flag tombstones lag behind real usage so tenants exceed ceilings without enforcement
stressors.solution: Pre-aggregation and bounded admission with shed-by-class: quota_aggregator pre-aggregates usage deltas in-memory by (tenant, plan_version, tenant_cluster, HLC bucket) before proposing to aggregate_lane, so consensus throughput scales with aggregation buckets not raw delta count. When pre-aggregation buffer exceeds a documented watermark, low-severity deltas (well under per-plan ceiling) are dropped with a loss-attestation while near-ceiling and ceiling-crossing aggregates retain priority and are admitted to aggregate_lane preferentially

stressors.description: Inter-region channel cert-rotation chicken-and-egg: the cert-bearing channel that hlc_service uses for sample exchange and quorum_core uses for inter-region replication is itself rotated by lifecycle_gate via control_lane consensus, which depends on the very channel being rotated
stressors.attractor: Cert rotation proposed via control_lane requires consensus over the cert-bearing channel; if rotation is required because old certs are about to expire, the rotation cannot commit before expiry — system enters a state where consensus is impossible because no channel authenticates
stressors.solution: Overlapping cert validity with proactive rotation budget: lifecycle_gate enforces that cert rotations on the inter-region channel are admitted only when the remaining validity exceeds a documented overlap window, during which the new cert is trusted alongside the old; the new cert is distributed via control_lane while consensus still rides on the old cert; trust handover is atomic at the HLC effective-from. If the overlap window is breached (rotation could not commit in time), lifecycle_gate raises an emergency-cert-recovery event and the parent operator path takes over via an out-of-band cert-bootstrap surface (bubbled to parent)

stressors.description: HLC drift during legitimate region pause (VM live migration): a paused region's hlc_service falls behind multi-peer median; on resume, the region trips skew-degraded mode even though there was no actual time-sync misbehavior, just a documented operational pause
stressors.attractor: Live-migration pause causes false skew-degraded mode: the migrated region rejects writes for the documented degraded-mode window unnecessarily; rolling live-migrations across regions cascade into avoidable degraded-mode windows
stressors.solution: Pause-aware HLC sample bounds: lifecycle_gate publishes pause-in-progress events into control_lane for documented operational pauses (live migration is a recognized pause class); hlc_service consults control_lane for pause-in-progress entries scoped to its region — during a pause window, sample-vs-median delta is evaluated against a wider pause-mode bound, and on resume the region re-syncs from multi-peer median before re-entering normal acceptance, without triggering skew-degraded mode

stressors.description: Cross-lane HLC stamp inconsistency under hlc_service degradation: SR1-cross-lane-ordering relies on HLC stamps captured at write-time, but if hlc_service is degraded or unavailable, write-time stamps may be unreliable or missing, breaking happens-before reconstruction for revocation-then-attestation chains
stressors.attractor: Lane writes accepted with stale or missing HLC stamps; consumers reconstructing happens-before across lanes (e.g. revocation in tombstone_lane preceding flag-applied attestation in control_lane) infer wrong order; security-critical orderings violated
stressors.solution: Mandatory HLC stamping with degraded-mode interlock: every lane entry's HLC stamp is validated at quorum_core commit time against the current HLC and rejected if missing or beyond max-allowed-delta. While hlc_service is in skew-degraded mode for the leader's region, quorum_core stops admitting writes that depend on time-bucketed enforcement (already a partial req) AND stops admitting any entry kind that participates in cross-lane happens-before reconstruction (security-critical orderings). The remaining admissions carry an HLC-degraded annotation visible to consumers

stressors.description: Source quarantine bypass via colluding sources: multi-source fork admission requires N independent observations, but a small set of colluding chain_router replicas can co-submit fabricated head observations; per-source rate limit is per-replica, so multiple replicas multiply the attack budget. Quarantine logic requires single-source pattern violations
stressors.attractor: Coordinated multi-replica fabrication admits a malicious (chain, fork_id) over the N-region threshold; canonical-tip view contaminated; reorgs emitted on a non-existent fork
stressors.solution: Region-distinct independence requirement and cross-source correlation widening: tip_quorum's N independent observations for fork admission require sources from N distinct regions (not N distinct replicas in the same region); cross-source-correlation rules widen from per-source pattern to set-level — if a fork_id is admitted only by replicas in suspicious correlation (synchronized timing, identical observation deltas, no other regional witness), the entire correlated set is held in probationary even if no single source violates per-source rate

stressors.description: Residency two-phase activation across an HLC-degraded region: phase-2 activation is globally-ordered via HLC, but a region in skew-degraded mode has stopped accepting writes that depend on time-bucketed enforcement; this could either block activation indefinitely or activate inconsistently across regions
stressors.attractor: Tightening residency change either stalls (degraded region cannot acknowledge readiness, blocks activation) or activates with the degraded region serving stale policy past activation HLC; either way, the deny-by-default fallback applies broadly when the cause is just operational degradation

stressors.description: best-effort attestation cascade under sustained downstream outage: a downstream component (e.g. fanout) is down for an extended window; offboarding_orchestrator records best-effort attestations on every offboarding for that component; certificate-of-deletion 'complete-with-exceptions' state becomes the norm rather than the exception; exceptions register grows unbounded; SLA on resolution becomes meaningless
stressors.attractor: Sustained downstream outage transforms 'complete-with-exceptions' from an edge case into a default state; certification audit trail loses signal because exceptions accumulate without back-pressure
stressors.solution: Component-outage circuit breaker: offboarding_orchestrator tracks best-effort attestation rate per downstream component; when the rate exceeds a documented breaker threshold, offboarding_orchestrator stops issuing new offboarding signals to that component and surfaces a component-outage alert; new erasure tombstones for tenants whose data class touches that component are held in a 'queued-pending-component-recovery' state in tombstone_lane rather than being rapidly converted to best-effort attestations; complete-with-exceptions remains a true exception state

stressors.description: Audit-key destruction PHASE B for tenant T commits (lease-lane DESTROYED entry) while lease_issuer is mid-handoff-fence for the SAME tenant T to a successor writer: lease_issuer's handoff-fence-ack from tenant_store is in flight, lease_v_new not yet activated. PHASE B's t_destroy was computed from observed_ack_hlc covering the prior writer's drain-ack-HLC, but the NEW writer (lease_v_new holder) hasn't started writing yet — once activated it may emit audit writes whose encrypted-at-HLC > the prior writer's drain-ack-HLC for T. compliance_audit_owner's late-write cutoff is per (writer_id, encrypted-at-HLC); the new writer is a different writer_id but its writes for T arrive AFTER DESTROYED. The cutoff installed at DESTROYED commit doesn't cover the new writer's writes for T because (writer_id_new, *) was never bounded, so the writes are admitted but the audit-key for T is destroyed, rendering them unreadable: silent data loss for what should be terminal-state writes.
stressors.attractor: System drifts toward a state where audit-key destruction is treated as terminal for the prior writer set but the lease-handoff successor writer set is unbounded — late writes from the successor land in compliance_audit, get encrypted with a destroyed key, and become unreadable noise. Tenant erasure attestation is issued claiming complete-with-exceptions, but a residual stream of unreadable audit entries continues to land for the (now-erased) tenant. Operators cannot distinguish the residual stream from an attack.
stressors.solution: lifecycle_gate's PHASE B audit-key destruction must observe a no-active-lease invariant for tenant T at t_destroy: t_destroy is admitted only when lease_issuer reports there is no active or prepared lease for T (every lease for T is in revoked or superseded-and-flushed terminal state) AND no in-flight handoff-fence for T. lease_issuer publishes a per-tenant lease-quiescent flag to control_lane that lifecycle_gate's PHASE B CAS proposal includes as a precondition. Erasure-tombstone in tombstone_lane for tenant T causes lease_issuer to force-revoke any active lease for T as part of the drain-fence broadcast pipeline, and to refuse handoff-fence requests for T (handoff during erasure is invalid by construction); the lease-quiescent flag flips only after force-revocation commits and any in-flight handoff is either completed or aborted. compliance_audit_owner's late-write cutoff is broadened from (writer_id, encrypted-at-HLC) to (any writer with active or prepared lease for T at any HLC up to t_destroy) — the cutoff is a tenant-key-scoped admission predicate, not a per-writer HLC bound. Late writes from any writer for T after DESTROYED are rejected at admission and surfaced to the protocol-violation log.

stressors.description: residency_publisher's V+1 COMMIT (M-of-regions activation CAS) is in flight while credential_roster's rotation-activate for roster_v_new commits first. residency_publisher's COMMIT proposal carries the prior roster_version captured at PREPARE time; CAS-rejects with 'roster-version-stale' reason because the activation broadcast says active roster is now newer. residency_publisher must abort V+1 — but tenant_store is in V+1-prepared state with HLC-bounded prepared-window. Abort fires under (tenant_key, V+1, attempt_id) idempotency. Operator retries V+1 PREPARE with a new attempt_id. Now residency_publisher's new PREPARE carries roster_v_new captured at retry time; tenant_store sees back-to-back PREPARE attempts for the same V+1 with different attempt_ids; quarantine-and-relocate state may still be observable from prior attempt; tenant_store's idempotent relocate-and-rollback may have rolled back AFTER the second PREPARE landed, leaving the second PREPARE in V+1-prepared state but with V's data already partially relocated. The HLC ordering is well-defined but tenant_store's internal state-machine is now a stack of V+1-prepared attempts that did or did not commit; residency_publisher's COMMIT for the second attempt may succeed against a tenant_store state that was left in a half-rolled-back configuration by the first abort.
stressors.attractor: Stack of V+1-prepared attempts in tenant_store, each tagged with distinct attempt_id, with quarantine-and-relocate state in indeterminate partial-rollback configuration. Operators see PREPARED-ORPHAN alarms from prior aborts not yet fully reconciled when the next attempt's COMMIT lands; tenant_store's residency state may resolve to V+1 against partially-relocated data. Worst case: residency policy_version transition succeeds against a tenant_store state where some records are at V's residency, some at V+1's, with no clean diff.
stressors.solution: residency_publisher's CAS proposals (PREPARE, COMMIT, ABORT) MUST acquire a per-tenant residency 2PC lock at lifecycle_gate via control_lane: a tenant T enters residency-2PC-in-flight state on PREPARE commit and exits only on COMMIT, ABORT, or PREPARED-ORPHAN. While in-flight, no further PREPARE for the same tenant T is admitted; lifecycle_gate CAS-rejects competing PREPARE proposals with reason 'residency-2PC-already-in-flight'. The lock is HLC-bounded (matches the prepared-window) and auto-releases on PREPARED-ORPHAN. PREPARED-ORPHAN is a terminal state per (tenant_key, V+1) tuple — not per attempt_id; the same tenant_key cannot escape PREPARED-ORPHAN via a fresh attempt_id. Recovery from PREPARED-ORPHAN requires explicit operator action under M-of-N elevated threshold AND tenant_store reporting clean-rollback-complete. Roster-version capture for residency 2PC: PREPARE captures the active roster_version and pins it; COMMIT and ABORT carry the pinned roster_version. Roster rotation activations during in-flight residency 2PC are sequenced by lifecycle_gate: rotation-activate is admitted only after all in-flight residency 2PCs reach terminal state under the prior roster, OR the activation explicitly carries a residency-2PC-cancel-and-abort directive that issues idempotent abort-V+1 entries for every in-flight 2PC before activating the new roster — the directive itself requires elevated M-of-N.

stressors.description: A region-failover event causes correlated cold-start of every gateway/edge/usage_meter/metrics_store instance in the failed-over-to region: hundreds to thousands of new instance_ids registering simultaneously. Each requests pre-warm hydration from residency_publisher to ack-ready the active policy_version. Per-region rate limit caps throughput; the pre-warm queue overflows almost immediately; the bulk of new instances receive pre-warm-deferred and fall to deny-by-default for residency-pinned operations. Tenants whose residency policy pins them to the failed-over-to region see widespread denials for as long as the queue is draining. Per-region propagation budget is sized for steady-state churn, not for failover bursts.
stressors.attractor: Region-failover triggers a self-inflicted DoS: the failed-over-to region's freshly-spawned instances cannot serve residency-pinned traffic for tenants pinned to that region until the pre-warm queue drains, which is the same scenario the failover was supposed to mitigate. Operators see a flood of pre-warm-stalled alerts; tenant traffic shifts BACK to the failing-over-from region, undoing the failover's intent.
stressors.solution: Pre-warm hydration has two-tier admission: a per-region steady-state RPS cap for routine churn AND a region-failover burst-mode admission that activates when residency_publisher observes a quorum-witnessed region-failover event in control_lane. In burst-mode, the per-region RPS cap is replaced by a per-region burst-budget sized to absorb the documented worst-case correlated-cold-start population for the region, with HLC-bounded burst window matching the failover RTO. Pre-warm hydration uses bulk-snapshot delivery in burst-mode: instead of per-instance synchronous full-state delivery, residency_publisher publishes the active policy_version's full state once to a region-local cache (cert-bearing) and instances pull from the local cache, ack-readying inline. The local cache is itself a residency_publisher endpoint, monotonic-per-(consumer, instance_id, version), with the same deny-by-default semantics on cache miss. Burst-mode terminates when the failover RTO HLC window closes; instances arriving after the window fall back to per-region steady-state RPS cap. residency_publisher writes a burst-mode-active and burst-mode-terminate event to control_lane bracketing the burst window so operators can observe the boundary.

stressors.description: A writer's drain-ack-handoff record is committed to lease_lane naming a 'persistent buffer' instance as the successor that owns residual writes for tenant T. The buffer is a separate runtime instance with its own deployment lifecycle. Hours later, the buffer instance is itself decommissioned (e.g., the cluster is being completely retired) without flushing the residual writes. lifecycle_gate's PHASE B audit-key DESTROYED for T already committed (since the handoff-record was treated as ack-by-handoff), and compliance_audit_owner's tenant-key-scoped late-write cutoff is in place. The residual writes never get flushed. Certificate-of-deletion was issued in 'complete-with-exceptions' state with the handoff-record listed as the exception, but the actual data persists in the now-decommissioned buffer's storage (or was lost). Tenant erasure is officially complete; the data ALSO disappeared, but neither outcome is verified — the handoff-ack-by-handoff was a promise the system never enforced.
stressors.attractor: drain-ack-handoff becomes a 'kicked-can' admission shortcut: writers under teardown pressure routinely emit handoff records to satisfy ack semantics rather than completing flush. The exception register accumulates handoff entries that never resolve. Tenant erasure attestation degrades from a hard guarantee to a paper guarantee — auditors are told erasure is complete, but the actual erasure correctness depends on whether the named buffer ever flushed, which the system doesn't track end-to-end.
stressors.solution: drain-ack-handoff records are first-class durable obligations with their own SLA-tracked lifecycle, not closure of the original drain-fence ack: each handoff record commits to lease_lane in pending-flush state with an HLC-bounded flush deadline; the named successor instance acknowledges acceptance of the obligation by writing a handoff-accepted entry referencing the record-id; on flush completion the successor commits a handoff-flushed entry containing the actual flushed-write attestation; on deadline expiry without handoff-flushed, lifecycle_gate raises a handoff-overdue alarm and the certificate-of-deletion exception register entry escalates from 'handoff-pending' to 'handoff-overdue-investigation-required'. compliance_audit_owner's late-write cutoff for tenant T is NOT installed at PHASE B DESTROYED time — it is installed only after every handoff record for T has reached handoff-flushed terminal state OR has been explicitly resolved-with-loss-attestation under operator M-of-N (declaring the residual writes lost-and-accepted). PHASE B audit-key DESTROYED commits before handoff resolution only if the handoff record explicitly carries a no-residual-writes-expected flag — true only when the writer's flush-then-ack-then-teardown ordering completed without unflushed writes (the handoff is a no-op record retained for audit completeness, not an actual obligation). Decommissioning a successor buffer is itself a lifecycle event admitted by lifecycle_gate that requires ALL pending-flush handoff records the buffer owns to be either resolved or transferred-to-another-successor (a recursive handoff that re-applies the same SLA contract).

stressors.description: gateway_health_surface receives a routing-affecting Subrole transition (gateway-active -> fanout-suspended) from region A. Region B's gateway_health_surface samples never arrive within the cross-witness window because of an asymmetric partition between region B's gateway_health_surface and region A's quorum_core leader. Other regions are healthy but their samples for region A's Subrole are stale (regions don't sample each other's Subroles directly — each region samples its own Subroles and publishes; cross-witnessing requires multiple regions to AGREE on what they observe of region A). The classification stays in cross-witness-pending past the documented window and is rejected with an alert. edge continues routing as if region A's fanout is fully active. Subscriptions are sent to region A's fanout, which is actually suspended, so they queue or fail. Reconnect storm hints are not emitted because the classification was rejected. Tenants in region A see opaque subscription failures with no health-surface signal that region A is degraded.
stressors.attractor: Cross-witness becomes a single-point-of-failure for routing: any partition that prevents inter-region health agreement masks degradation rather than surfacing it. Operators see 'classification-rejected' alerts but no actionable Subrole status; tenants in the actually-degraded region experience failures while edge continues routing under stale liveness.
stressors.solution: Cross-witness is a defense against forged or buggy single-region classifications, not a routing-correctness gate. gateway_health_surface promotes a single-region classification to cross-witness-pending with explicit annotation, AND publishes the classification-pending entry to health_lane with the single observing region named so edge can apply a documented partial-trust policy: edge SHALL treat single-region routing-affecting classifications as advisory — for routing-affecting transitions in the safety direction (more conservative, e.g. fanout-suspended), edge applies the classification immediately under partial-trust with a 'partial-trust-routing-active' header on outgoing requests; for transitions in the permissive direction (less conservative, e.g. fanout-suspended -> gateway-active), edge requires full cross-witness before applying. The cross-witness window is a tunable: if expired with no second witness, the classification escalates to operator-attention rather than being silently rejected. lifecycle_gate may issue an operator-override classification (under M-of-N) that promotes a single-region classification past the window with operator attribution.

stressors.description: cert_bootstrap's OOB anchor is M-of-N hardware-rooted material with anchor-availability-test cadence. The cadence is set conservatively (weekly). Two anchor elements silently fail BETWEEN tests: a hardware module loses its key material due to firmware corruption, and another's custodian organization has a personnel change that renders the anchor element inaccessible. Neither failure is detected for days. An emergency arises (inter-region channel cert effectively expired before in-band rotation could commit); cert_bootstrap attempts emergency cert recovery under elevated M-of-N; only N-2 anchor elements are reachable; M-of-N quorum is unreachable; emergency cert recovery cannot proceed. region_coordinator's inter-region channel is dead; consensus is unavailable; the entire control plane is in 'frozen' state. Worse: emergency lease re-bootstrap (which uses a different elevated threshold) might still be reachable with N-2 elements, creating an asymmetric recovery state where lease ops can re-bootstrap but the inter-region channel that lease ops require is itself dead.
stressors.attractor: Anchor-availability-test cadence becomes a measurement of false confidence: weekly tests reassure operators that the anchor is healthy, but the actual emergency-recovery surface depends on instantaneous reachability that the test cadence cannot capture. Recovery becomes a question of luck — whether the most recent test caught the silent failure. Multiple silent failures compound to render emergency recovery permanently unavailable; the only path forward is to accept loss of the inter-region channel and rebuild from external trust roots that may not exist.
stressors.solution: Anchor-availability is monitored continuously, not just at test cadence: each anchor custodian publishes a heartbeat-attestation to control_lane on a documented sub-test-cadence interval (per-anchor-element heartbeat). cert_bootstrap maintains a per-anchor liveness state in control_lane; on missing heartbeat for documented intervals, the anchor element is marked anchor-unhealthy and an alarm is raised. M-of-N counts only anchor-healthy elements; if anchor-healthy count drops below M, an anchor-quorum-degraded alarm is raised PROACTIVELY (before any emergency arises) so operators can rotate-in a replacement anchor under the still-reachable healthy quorum. Anchor rotation is admitted by lifecycle_gate as a first-class lifecycle event subject to bounded-batching; replacement anchors join under the still-reachable elevated M-of-N. Emergency recovery thresholds are explicitly named in cert_bootstrap's definition and cannot be silently weakened: cert re-rooting and roster-bootstrap require elevated-tier-A; emergency lease re-bootstrap requires elevated-tier-B; both tiers reference M-of-N applied against anchor-healthy count, never against total anchor count, so degradation is monotonic — an anchor failure cannot accidentally lower the quorum requirement. anchor-availability-tests remain part of the cadence as a defense-in-depth check that the heartbeat is itself trustworthy.

stressors.description: A bulk-tenant-offboarding wave admits 5000 tenants. lifecycle_gate's drain-fence broadcast pipeline scales by bounded waves with documented max-tenants-per-wave (e.g. 100). For each tenant, lease_issuer must commit a force-revoke to lease_lane before the per-tenant lease-quiescent flag flips and PHASE B audit-key destruction can proceed. quorum_core enforces a per-proposer in-flight CAS budget on lease_issuer; with 100 force-revokes per wave, lease_issuer hits its budget and proposals queue. The per-tenant HLC-bounded ack window starts from per-tenant ack-broadcast-emit-HLC (good — bulk-load arrival smearing won't collapse windows), but the force-revoke commits ARE serialized through quorum_core's CAS budget, so tenants late in the wave see lease-quiescent flag flip well after their drain-fence ack window opens. Their drain-fences time out before their leases are revoked; lifecycle_gate's PHASE B precondition (lease-quiescent for T) is not met within the per-tenant ack window. The bulk wave produces a flood of partial-with-witnesses certificates of deletion (partial because lease-quiescent timed out). Operators see a sustained alert flood and the bulk-offboarding job degrades to single-tenant retries.
stressors.attractor: Bulk-offboarding becomes a coupled-throttling problem: drain-fence pipeline's bounded-batching is sized for ack fan-in throughput, but lease_issuer's CAS budget is sized for steady-state lease ops; the two budgets are not co-tuned. Operators see partial-with-witnesses certificates as the default outcome of bulk-offboarding rather than the exception state it was intended to be.
stressors.solution: lease_issuer publishes its current per-proposer in-flight CAS budget headroom to control_lane; lifecycle_gate's bulk-offboarding wave admission CAS proposal includes lease_issuer's CAS budget headroom as a precondition: a wave is admitted only when (lease_issuer.cas_budget_headroom >= max-tenants-per-wave) AND (every other named-writer's bounded queue depth >= max-tenants-per-wave). Wave admission is rejected with reason 'lease-issuer-budget-insufficient' or 'writer-queue-full' when the precondition fails; lifecycle_gate's bulk-admission backs off and retries with exponential-with-jitter. Force-revoke proposals from lease_issuer are admitted through a dedicated lease-revoke-during-erasure CAS sub-budget that is reserved within the lease_issuer per-proposer budget and not consumable by routine lease ops. lease_issuer publishes the dedicated sub-budget separately to control_lane so the bulk-admission precondition checks against the dedicated sub-budget headroom (not the total budget) — routine lease churn does not starve erasure-driven force-revocations.

stressors.description: A named writer's hlc_service is in skew-degraded mode at the moment it acks a drain-fence for tenant T. Its drain-ack-HLC is computed at the writer's local HLC. quorum_core's HLC-degraded interlock suspends admission of security-critical cross-lane orderings (revocation-then-attestation, erasure-tombstone-then-offboarding-attestation) for the leader's hlc_service in skew-degraded mode — but this is leader-side; a writer-side hlc_service in skew-degraded is not interlocked. The writer's drain-ack-HLC is therefore unreliable: it may be ahead of true real-time (clock drifted forward) or behind (drifted back). PHASE B uses observed_ack_hlc + skew_bound + write-delivery-grace; if drain-ack-HLC is ahead of real-time, PHASE B's t_destroy is too early and post-flush legitimate writes from the writer (made at correct real-time) are rejected as late. If drain-ack-HLC is behind, PHASE B is delayed and the audit-key destruction takes longer than the documented SLA.
stressors.attractor: Asymmetric trust in HLC: the leader's hlc_service has interlocks; the writer's does not. Erasure correctness becomes contingent on writer-side clock health that the protocol cannot directly observe. Either tenant erasure intermittently rejects legitimate flush attestations (false-positive cutoff) or audit-key destruction is silently delayed past SLA (false-negative completeness).
stressors.solution: drain-acks carry the writer's hlc_service status (healthy / skew-degraded / pause-mode) at ack-emission time as a typed annotation. offboarding_orchestrator REJECTS drain-acks emitted by writers whose hlc_service is in skew-degraded mode at ack-emission time: the ack is treated as not-acked-yet, and the writer must re-ack after its hlc_service has returned to healthy state. Writers whose hlc_service is in pause-mode emit drain-ack-pause-deferred records that ride the same flush-then-ack-then-teardown ordering but explicitly carry the pause-window HLC bounds; offboarding_orchestrator accepts drain-ack-pause-deferred as ack-by-handoff with the pause-window-end as the deferred-completion HLC, and lifecycle_gate's PHASE B does not commit until the pause-window has ended and a healthy-mode drain-ack lands. lifecycle_gate's PHASE B t_destroy computation uses observed_ack_hlc only when EVERY contributing drain-ack was emitted under healthy hlc_service; otherwise t_destroy is computed from the worst-case drain-ack-pause-deferred completion HLC + skew_bound + write-delivery-grace. Writers cannot fake healthy-status: hlc_service status annotations are signed by the writer's hlc_service over the cert-bearing inter-region channel and verified by offboarding_orchestrator before the ack is admitted.

stressors.description: credential_roster commits a compromise-revocation event with retroactive-as-of-HLC set significantly earlier than the revocation HLC (forensics established compromise predates discovery by 12 hours). lifecycle_gate must re-sign and re-broadcast every in-flight drain-fence broadcast whose emit-HLC >= retroactive-as-of-HLC. During those 12 hours, several bulk-offboarding waves were admitted with thousands of drain-fence broadcasts. Re-sign-and-rebroadcast all of them respects bounded-batching, but the bounded-batching budget is sized for the next-incoming bulk wave, not for re-emission. The re-emission queue saturates lifecycle_gate's broadcast pipeline; new incoming bulk-offboarding requests are stalled; per-tenant ack windows for the re-emitted broadcasts are reset, but the original ack windows had already partially completed for many tenants — those tenants' phase markers are at FLUSH-COMPLETE or ACK-EMITTED with the OLD signing roster_version. Per the no-retract semantics, those acks stay valid; the re-emission creates a parallel ack pipeline for the same tenants. Operators see double-ack noise; some tenants ack once for the new broadcast, some don't (they already finished); offboarding_orchestrator must reconcile two parallel ack streams per tenant.
stressors.attractor: Compromise-revocation with deep retroactive-as-of-HLC becomes a duplication storm rather than a clean re-validation. Operators face double-counting of acks, ambiguous certificate-of-deletion state for the re-emission window, and a stalled new-wave admission queue. The system trades one security incident (compromised credential) for an operational incident (stuck bulk pipeline), tempting operators to set retroactive-as-of-HLC closer to revocation HLC than forensics actually justifies.
stressors.solution: Re-sign-and-rebroadcast does NOT reset per-tenant ack windows for tenants whose broadcast had already reached an ack-completed phase (FLUSH-COMPLETE, ACK-EMITTED, ATTESTATION-WRITTEN, or TERMINAL) at the original signing — those acks remain valid; lifecycle_gate's re-emission carries a per-tenant signature-only-update annotation that updates the broadcast's signing roster_version in offboarding_orchestrator's phase marker registry without resetting the ack window. Only tenants whose broadcasts had not reached an ack-completed phase get a fresh ack window with the re-signed broadcast. Re-emission has its own dedicated bandwidth budget within lifecycle_gate's broadcast pipeline (separate from new-wave admission), sized as a fraction of total broadcast pipeline capacity to bound the impact on new-wave admission. credential_roster's compromise-revocation broadcast carries an explicit reaffirmation-or-reissue per-tenant decision tree: tenants whose phase markers are ack-completed under the old signature receive a reaffirmation entry (signature update only); tenants whose markers are not yet ack-completed receive a reissue with fresh ack window. compliance_audit_owner records the reaffirmation-or-reissue decision per tenant in the typed audit log so the certificate-of-deletion can vouch for the signature transition without ambiguity.

stressors.description: residency_publisher's PREPARE for a tenant with massive data (e.g., 100GB sharded across regions) requires tenant_store's quarantine-and-relocate to complete before tenant_store emits prepared-ack. The quarantine-and-relocate is data-volume-dependent and can take far longer than the documented HLC-bounded prepared-window for routine tenants. Prepared-window expires before prepared-ack arrives; PREPARED-ORPHAN fires; tenant enters degraded mode requiring operator M-of-N to recover. Every operator-driven residency-tightening for any large-data tenant becomes an operator escalation event rather than an automated transition.
stressors.attractor: Large tenants become structurally unable to use automated residency-tightening: every transition requires elevated operator action, defeating the automation. Operators eventually configure a uniform 'large enough for everyone' prepared-window which is wasteful for routine tenants and still insufficient for the largest, with a manual-override workflow becoming the de-facto path.
stressors.solution: residency_publisher's prepared-window is per-(tenant_key, V+1) and dynamically sized based on tenant_store's per-tenant data-volume estimate captured at PREPARE time: tenant_store reports an estimated_quarantine_duration in a preliminary PREPARE-estimate exchange before the PREPARE proposal commits; residency_publisher computes the prepared-window as max(min-window, estimated_duration * documented_safety_margin), capped at a documented absolute-max-window. If tenant_store cannot produce an estimate within a documented budget, residency_publisher uses the documented worst-case window. The estimate is bounded above and below by per-tenant quotas published in control_lane so a misreport from a single tenant_store replica cannot trivially extend a prepared-window to defeat the safety contract. PREPARED-ORPHAN remains the safety net for genuine stalls beyond absolute-max-window. tenant_store progress reports during quarantine-and-relocate write to control_lane (via region_coordinator's parent writes_to edge); residency_publisher monitors progress and may explicitly extend the prepared-window once before absolute-max-window is reached if progress is observable, with the extension itself committed as a prepared-window-extended entry to control_lane and operator-visible.

stressors.description: Compound failure across the v5 cluster: an operator initiates a bulk-offboarding wave; lifecycle_gate's broadcast pipeline is saturated emitting drain-fence + audit-key destruction PHASE A entries; meanwhile residency_publisher has multiple in-flight 2PC PREPAREs (with roster-pin); and one writer has a drain-ack-handoff-record stuck in pending-flush state past handoff-overdue-investigation-required SLA. offboarding_orchestrator must produce a per-tenant certificate-of-deletion. What does it say about a tenant whose handoff-record never resolved, whose residency 2PC was forcibly aborted mid-PREPARE, and whose audit-key destruction is paused at PHASE A awaiting late-write cutoff confirmation? Today, no rule says what truth state the certificate carries, and downstream consumers (compliance_audit_owner) must accept or reject it.
stressors.attractor: System drifts toward issuing certificates-of-deletion that mix terminal facts (residency aborted, audit-key still live, handoff lost) with no normative status field — compliance_audit_owner stores them, but downstream re-attestations surface contradictions weeks later when handoff-overdue-investigation-required investigations close with resolved-with-loss-attestation. Operators learn the deletion is partial only via audit drift, not at the moment of certificate issuance.
stressors.solution: offboarding_orchestrator must emit a structured certificate-of-deletion with explicit deletion_status enum (CLEAN | PARTIAL_HANDOFF_LOSS | RESIDENCY_ABORTED | AUDIT_KEY_PHASE_A_PENDING | COMPOUND), required terminal-fact roll-up (per-component phase markers, residency 2PC outcome, audit-key phase, handoff-record SLA terminal state), and a refusal to issue a certificate while ANY handoff-record SLA is non-terminal unless an explicit operator-attested resolved-with-loss-attestation override is present. compliance_audit_owner must reject any certificate missing this roll-up. lifecycle_gate broadcast pipeline must shed-and-defer non-critical PHASE A entries when residency 2PC PREPAREs are above watermark, with explicit deferral records in control_lane so audit-key destruction does not stall silently.

stressors.description: lease_lane head-of-line blocking: a long-running M-of-regions lease-prepared ack-collection (with one slow region) holds the head of lease_lane while a bulk-offboarding wave drives a flood of lease-revoked entries that must commit ahead of erasure-tombstone fanout. Lease_lane's reserved consensus throughput is single-stream; lease-revoked under bulk-offboarding shares the same lane. Slow region's ack delays the prepared entry; downstream lease-revoked commits are stalled, leaving leases live past their must-revoke deadline; gateway_health_surface and edge keep accepting traffic against tenants whose erasure tombstone was already emitted.
stressors.attractor: Operators learn the system silently keeps live leases past must-revoke deadlines under bulk-offboarding when any region is slow on lease-prepared. Workaround attempts (operator force-revoke at tier-A) compound by jumping the queue and orphaning prepared-but-not-yet-acked entries, leaving lease_issuer with a permanent prepared-orphan backlog.
stressors.solution: lease_lane MUST split into two priority classes within reserved consensus throughput: (1) lease-revoke-priority sub-stream (lease-revoked, lease-revoke-during-erasure, force-revoke) bypasses lease-prepared entries with a strict ordering rule (revoke for tenant T overrides any prepared for T), and (2) lease-prepared sub-stream serializes M-of-regions ack-collection. lease_issuer MUST emit prepared-orphan entries when a force-revoke supersedes a prepared, with a bounded reaper. lease-prepared MUST carry an admission-deadline-HLC; expired prepared entries become prepared-expired and are reaped, freeing lane head. lifecycle_gate bulk-wave admission MUST budget against lease-revoke-priority throughput, not total lane throughput.

stressors.description: health_lane vs lease_lane cross-witness window race: gateway_health_surface marks region R's Subroles down at HLC=t while a lease-revoke-priority commit for tenant T (whose live lease was issued in R) lands in lease_lane at HLC=t±epsilon. v5's asymmetric partial-trust policy says safety-direction is immediate, but partial-trust headers on edge requests for already-revoked leases live in a window where edge has not yet seen lease-revoke (lease_lane fanout) but has seen partial-trust (health_lane fanout). edge admits a request under partial-trust on a revoked lease. There is no cross-lane HLC barrier between health_lane down-witness and lease_lane lease-revoke for the same (tenant, region).
stressors.attractor: Auditors find time-bounded windows where partial-trust requests against already-revoked leases were admitted; remediation by widening cross-witness window pessimistically increases tail latency on every health flap. Operators learn the asymmetric policy was undefined for cross-lane events at the same HLC bucket.
stressors.solution: gateway_health_surface MUST NOT publish a partial-trust safety-direction transition for region R until cross-witnessing lease_lane up to HLC=transition_hlc is confirmed (lease-revoke-priority entries for any tenant whose lease names region R must be ordered-before the partial-trust publication). A partial-trust transition for R carries a lease_lane-cross-witnessed-up-to HLC, and edge MUST refuse to apply a partial-trust header for R until edge has also observed lease_lane up to that HLC. lease_issuer MUST stamp lease-revoke entries with the originating-region-set so health_lane can identify which leases are within scope of an R-down transition.

stressors.description: quorum_core HLC-degraded interlock: in v2 the HLC-degraded interlock was defined for security-critical cross-lane orderings, but the new v4/v5 lanes (lease_lane lease-prepared, lease-revoke; health_lane classification-pending, partial-trust-transition) have not been classified into the interlock set. Under HLC degradation, lease-prepared without HLC-bounded ordering can race lease-revoked-with-erasure, allowing a prepared lease to commit AFTER its revoke for the same tenant. health_lane partial-trust transitions can publish without HLC stamps and override safety-direction transitions out of order. A pause-mode region during HLC skew can have its lease-prepared admitted by a peer that has not seen the pause.
stressors.attractor: Under sustained HLC skew, the architecture drifts toward an undefined regime for the new lanes: operators see anomalies (revoked leases admitted; partial-trust order inverted) without a single guard that fails-closed. Workarounds add per-event ad-hoc HLC checks in the new subservices, fragmenting the interlock contract.
stressors.solution: quorum_core's HLC-degraded interlock MUST classify lease_lane (lease-prepared, lease-revoke, lease-revoke-during-erasure, force-revoke, prepared-orphan, prepared-expired) and health_lane (partial-trust-transition, classification-pending, classification-witness-timeout, anchor-quorum-degraded) as security-critical. Under HLC-degraded mode, security-critical entries on these lanes MUST be suspended (NOT committed) and a deferral record written; lease-revoke for tenant T retains its priority but MUST be HLC-stamp-revalidated against hlc_service before commit. health_lane partial-trust transitions under HLC-degraded MUST be downgraded to safety-direction-only (no permissive direction) and carry an hlc-degraded-source flag so consumers know the cross-witness stamp is provisional.

stressors.description: A compromise-revocation broadcast (lifecycle_gate retroactive-as-of-HLC) demands re-signing of all in-flight credentials and reissuance of every lease bound to the compromised roster_version. The lease_lane is currently saturated with lease-prepared M-of-regions ack-collection. credential_roster's per-tenant reaffirmation-or-reissue tree fires, but the resulting lease-reissue write storm collides with the lease-revoke-priority sub-stream (introduced in s4-2). With elevated-tier-A directives also queued for residency-2PC-cancel-and-abort, lease_issuer cannot keep up; reissue lag grows. Worse, lease-prepared entries pinned to the compromised roster_version are still in flight and might commit under the old roster after the compromise is broadcast.
stressors.attractor: System enters a state where revocation broadcast outpaces reissue capacity; operators see protracted windows where new leases cannot be issued (gateway-unavailable for affected tenants) yet old prepared-but-not-committed leases under the compromised roster could still commit, breaching the security promise of compromise-revocation.
stressors.solution: lease_issuer MUST atomically invalidate all lease-prepared entries bound to a compromised roster_version on receipt of compromise-revocation broadcast: such prepared entries transition immediately to prepared-revoked (a new state distinct from prepared-orphan and prepared-expired) and MUST NOT be allowed to commit even if M-of-regions acks arrive afterward. credential_roster's reaffirmation-or-reissue decision tree MUST emit reissue work into a third lease_lane sub-stream (lease-reissue), distinct from lease-revoke-priority and lease-prepared, with its own bounded budget; lease-reissue MUST be ordered after the compromise-revocation broadcast HLC and MUST NOT be ordered before any lease-revoke for the same tenant. lifecycle_gate MUST surface a back-pressure signal to operators when lease-reissue budget saturates beyond a configurable horizon.

stressors.description: Bulk-offboarding wave produces synchronized health-down witnesses across many regions (e.g., a tenant with presence in 50 regions, all witnessing each others health degradation during teardown-overlap). health_lane fills with classification-pending entries faster than gateway_health_surface can clear them within the cross-witness window; classification-witness-timeout pages on-call escalate as a flood. Meanwhile classification-pending entries pile up under HLC-degraded interlock (s4-4) deferral. Operators cannot distinguish actual region-health flaps from bulk-offboarding-correlated witnesses.
stressors.attractor: On-call drowns in classification-witness-timeout pages during every bulk-offboarding wave; operators eventually mute health_lane alerts during planned waves, masking real region-health flaps and breaking the freshness SLO that gateway_health_surface promises.
stressors.solution: gateway_health_surface MUST tag every classification-pending and partial-trust-transition entry on health_lane with the originating-cause-class (operator-bulk-wave, regional-network, internal-degradation, unknown) sourced from lifecycle_gate's bulk-wave context. Entries tagged operator-bulk-wave MUST be subject to a separate classification-witness-timeout SLO (longer, no individual paging) and aggregated into a single bulk-wave-health-summary published once per wave; only deviations from the wave's expected health envelope page on-call. lifecycle_gate MUST publish bulk-wave start/end markers on control_lane carrying the (offboarding_id, wave_id, expected-region-set) so health_lane consumers can correlate without ad-hoc heuristics.

stressors.description: drain-fence broadcast triggered by lifecycle_gate during a bulk-wave lands while residency_publisher's in-flight residency 2PC PREPARE is roster-pinned to roster_version V_old (pinned at PREPARE), and offboarding_orchestrator's open handoff-records also reference V_old. Mid-flight, credential_roster sequences a rotation-activate to V_new; the drain-fence carrying signing roster_version is signed under V_new but the in-flight 2PC is still pinned to V_old. The compound: drain-fence-V_new arrives at a writer that is mid-PREPARE-ack to residency_publisher under V_old; the writer's drain-ack-handoff record is signed under V_old (per its lease and the residency lock); compliance_audit_owner sees a roster mismatch on terminal records and cannot verify the chain of custody.
stressors.attractor: Audit chain-of-custody verification across roster rotation becomes statistically lossy during bulk waves; compliance_audit_owner's late-write cutoff cannot be installed cleanly because handoff records and PREPARE records are signed under different rosters, with no cross-version verification rule. Operators learn after the fact via failed audit replays.
stressors.solution: lifecycle_gate's rotation-activate sequencing MUST take effect at the boundary of in-flight residency 2PCs and open handoff-records: the activation HLC MUST be recorded such that any record signed before the activation HLC verifies under V_old and any record after verifies under V_new, with an explicit cross-version verification rule maintained by credential_roster (V_old remains verifiable for at least the residency-2PC-in-flight-lock max-window plus handoff-record SLA max-window). residency_publisher's roster-pin at PREPARE MUST include the rotation-activation-HLC visible at PREPARE; if a rotation-activate would land before the in-flight COMMIT, the 2PC MUST either complete before the activation or transition to residency-2PC-cancel-and-abort under elevated-tier-A. compliance_audit_owner MUST accept a chain-of-custody signed under V_old as long as the activation HLC and the V_old verification key are still in the bounded retention window. Drain-ack-handoff records MUST embed the roster_version under which they were signed AND the activation HLC observed at signing time.

stressors.description: Dual region failover: regions A and B both transition partial-trust simultaneously (each cross-witnessing the other). Per s4-3, gateway_health_surface stamps each transition with a lease_lane-cross-witnessed-up-to HLC. Region A's transition cross-witnesses lease_lane up to HLC=t_A which depends on entries originating from region B; region B's transition does the same in reverse. lease_lane lease-revoke-priority entries for tenants whose leases name BOTH A and B are stalled because lease_issuer in A and B are each waiting for the other's witness. Net effect: cross-witness barrier becomes a deadlock rather than a safety guard.
stressors.attractor: Dual-region failover events become the dominant production incident: an architectural safety property under single-region failover becomes a deadlock under dual-region failover. Operators learn this only after first such incident; mitigation forces operator-tier-A override on cross-witness barriers, eroding the safety guarantee.
stressors.solution: gateway_health_surface MUST detect cross-witness deadlock by monitoring the dependency graph of in-flight partial-trust transitions; on deadlock detection, the simultaneously-failing regions MUST be classified as a region-set-failover (not independent transitions) and a single coordinated transition MUST be issued whose cross-witness barrier is computed across the union (lease_lane HLC observed by quorum_core's quorum, not by either region individually). lease_issuer MUST emit lease-revoke entries for tenants in the region-set under quorum_core's commit, not under either failing region's local witness, to break the cycle. health_lane MUST carry an explicit region-set-failover entry kind with the union region-set so consumers apply a single barrier rather than two interlocking ones.
